page: Amazon Web Services r9gd.24xlarge is an arm64 memory-optimized virtual machine delivered via the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. The compute subsystem is driven by AWS Graviton processors, providing 96 dedicated physical cores across 96 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. With each core pinned at a 3.3 GHz frequency and one hardware thread per physical execution unit, execution pipelines avoid the resource contention patterns commonly associated with hyperthreaded environments.

System memory consists of 768.0 GB of RAM, offering an allocation of 8.0 GB per core. In addition to main system memory, the server bundles 5,700 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance store volume. This integrated storage delivers high-speed local block access for temporary scratch data or active database tables, circumventing network storage latency. Complementing the local I/O profile, the network interface supports a baseline throughput of 50 Gbps without incorporating discrete hardware accelerators.

From an architectural perspective, the pairing of custom Arm silicon with dense local NVMe storage provides high resource density per instance footprint. The dedicated single-thread-per-core configuration and generous memory ratio offer balanced throughput for data-heavy platforms. This configuration directly addresses the demands of large-scale in-memory key-value stores, distributed caches, transactional relational databases, and real-time big data analytics pipelines requiring high local I/O performance.
description: Amazon Web Services r9gd.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro System hypervisor and powered by AWS Graviton processors. The instance provides 96 physical cores across 96 vCPUs using an arm64 architecture, with a single hardware thread per core operating at 3.3 GHz. Memory provisioning includes 768 GB of total capacity, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-core allocation suitable for massive memory demands. For high-throughput local operations, the server integrates 5,700 GB of NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. It does not include discrete hardware accelerators such as GPUs. By employing custom Arm architecture with non-hyperthreaded physical cores and high-capacity direct-attached storage, this configuration balances compute efficiency with high data density. The r9gd.24xlarge fits workloads requiring high RAM-to-CPU ratios and low-latency disk access, including large in-memory databases, Redis deployments, real-time analytics engines, distributed caching clusters, and high-throughput transactional storage systems.
